        Injuries keep piling up for the San Francisco 49ers as star wide receiver Mike Evans left Monday night's game late in the first half with an Achilles injury and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Evans was listed as questionable heading into the primetime contest against the Commanders, but managed to play and caught 3 passes for 94 yards before leaving. He was grabbing his Achilles after making a catch.Head coach Kyle Shanahan noted this week that Evans was dealing with Achilles soreness. The wideout did not practice at all this week, which left his status for Week 6 firmly up in the air for a big NFC matchup.Evans did not practice at all this week, with reports noting that he was mostly working off to the side. 
The 33-year-old has a history of playing through injuries and has not missed a contest to this point despite missing time in practice. Last week, Evans missed Thursday's practice with his rib injury, but ended up playing in the Week 5 win over Seattle. That said, this is the first time all season that Evans missed the entire week of practice. Evans signed a three-year, $42.4 million deal with the 49ers at the start of free agency, snapping his 12-season tenure with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. So far, the future Hall of Fame receiver has been as advertised and is coming off his first 100-yard game of the season, hauling in seven balls for 113 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Seahawks. Through five games, Evans has caught 24 of his 34 targets for 326 yards and three touchdowns. 
The 49ers offense was already without fellow receivers Deebo Samuel Jr., who was ruled out with a hamstring injury, and Christian Kirk with a calf injury.

title: Why Paris Saint-Germain's clash with Barcelona could be peak UCL drama - CBS Sports
description: 'I think all the ingredients are in place for this to be one of the great games,' PSG midfielder Vitinha said
body:
'I think all the ingredients are in place for this to be one of the great games,' PSG midfielder Vitinha said

        Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Vitinha did not beat around the bush before Tuesday's clash with Barcelona. "I think," he said, "all the ingredients are in place for this to be one of the great games."The UEFA Champions League's format switch came with the promise that top-tier matchups would come as early as possible every season and on Tuesday, the competition seems poised to live up to its word. Two favorites to win the whole thing, PSG and Barcelona, will meet in the French capital in the first barometer of their abilities to go the distance but that is merely scratching the surface on the excitement around this particular game.PSG and Barcelona are not only amongst Europe's elites but they each boast a collection of world-renowned talent, all of whom are poised to showcase moments of excellence no matter which way the game swings. Players like Ousmane Dembele and Lamine Yamal are headliners for teams that prefer to entertain when they take to the pitch, making them must-watches on a regular basis. History proves that these two sides rarely ever cancel each other out, either. If anything, their similarities only bolster the sheer entertainment every time PSG and Barcelona match up, the pair responsible for several Champions League classics over the years.Tuesday's match is likely to be no exception. It is also on course to become the greatest league phase match ever staged if history even comes close to repeating itself.
Here's why Barcelona's trip to PSG is worth the watch.How to watch Paris Saint-Germain vs. Barcelona, oddsDate: Tuesday, Oct. 20 | Time: 3 p.m. ETLocation: Parc des Princes -- ParisLive stream: Paramount+Odds: Paris Saint-Germain +145; Draw +350; Barcelona +140Star-studded attackers on displayTrue to form for two teams contending for Europe's top club prize, PSG and Barcelona have each assembled an impressive collection of attacking talent who are worth watching on a regular basis. Their particular skillsets vary but one thing they all seem to have in common – none of them shy away from the limelight, and so several are poised to create a highlight-reel worthy moment on Tuesday at the Parc des Princes.The most notable among them, of course, is Barcelona's Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old has nine goals and 10 assists across all competitions to start the season, each goal contribution a reminder that he is already a generational talent even with much of his career ahead of him. His goal in Saturday's 5-2 win over Real Betis is no exception, his strike from the edge of the penalty area worth watching over and over. Yamal will be a central figure in Tuesday's game, the teenager essentially a make-or-break player for an aspirational Barcelona.
"The best way to stop Lamine Yamal is to keep the ball away from Barcelona," PSG manager Luis Enrique said Monday. "If he cannot get the ball, everything is calm. That would be ideal, but we know it won't be the case because it is difficult to play against Barcelona and Lamine Yamal. The way to defend a team with their quality is to be wary and approach it as a team. But it's not just Lamine. There's Raphinha, Pedri … there are a lot of top players."Enrique is right that Yamal is not Barcelona's only attacking threat – Raphinha has been a staple since Hansi Flick took over as head coach two seasons ago, while Anthony Gordon's addition this summer has helped. Flick's side's attacking output has increased year-over-year. Barcelona average 4.3 goals from 3.7 expected goals per game this season in LaLiga, up from 2.5 goals from 2.3 expected goals in the previous campaign.PSG have plenty of attacking might to call upon on Tuesday, too. Enrique's side splits the goalscoring responsibilities between a few players, including Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele and France international Desire Doue. Both scored in last week's 4-2 win at Manchester City, while Spain World Cup winner Ferran Torres leads their scoring charts in Ligue 1. Then there's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who might just be PSG's most dynamic player on his best days. It is entirely unpredictable which players will rise above the rest on Tuesday but one glance at the list of options tells enough of a story – one of them is bound to showcase the range of their abilities on Tuesday, likely to leave many in awe along the way.
Barcelona might finally be up for the taskAs PSG cruised to a win at City on Matchday 2, the back-to-back Champions League winners only bolstered their case as the team to beat in Europe for another year running. It is hard not to describe them as the favorites on Tuesday as a result but this time around, Barcelona might actually be able to go toe-to-toe with Enrique's dominant side.Since Flick took charge two years ago, Barcelona have lived and died by the sword. The manager's attack-minded style was supposed to compensate for a leaky back line and for the most part, the plan has worked, so much so that they have two domestic titles to show for it. Down the stretch in the Champions League where margins define games, though, their defense had proved costly, most notably in the 2024-25 semifinals in which Inter beat them 7-6 on aggregate. Things have taken a turn in the right direction in recent weeks, though, because Barcelona signed the one player who is essentially a magical solution – World Cup winner Rodri.The midfielder is well-known for his jack of all trades, master of all-like tendencies, a skillset that earned him the Ballon d'Or two years ago and the World Cup Golden Ball award this summer. He fills in the gaps that led Barcelona to concede some unimpressive goals over the last couple of years and should be up for the task of doing so against PSG on Tuesday. Like Yamal, Rodri will also be instrumental in Barcelona's ability to come out of Paris with three points.
"I imagine a beautiful battle [in midfield]," Pedri said. "Both midfields suffer more when they do not have the ball so whoever has the ball tomorrow will have an advantage. We arrive with a good dynamic and with confidence."Rodri's arrival, alongside Barcelona's bolstered attack, ultimately allows the visitors to test this season's big hypothesis at an early juncture of the campaign."It will be a good test for us to show how far we are [from PSG]," Flick said. "I would like my team to play with confidence, play brave and, of course, play together as a team. We did it in the last 11 games; now we play against, if you see the last two years, the best team in the world. For us, it's a good opportunity to show our level, show what we can do and [see] what we have to improve. After this match, we will also know a lot of things."
The game at its bestThere is sometimes a dissonance between what makes for an important match and what makes for an entertaining match but if history is anything to go by with PSG and Barcelona, it is one and the same for these teams. There will be something for everyone, no matter what exactly your preferred brand of fun happens to be.Enrique and Flick will do what they can to cancel out the other, a tactical chess match of sorts set to take place in Paris on Tuesday. Each coach is determined to embrace their own versions of an attack-minded style of play but in their pre-match remarks, both were willing to admit that shutting the other team out entirely is perhaps unrealistic. They seem prepared for the ebbs and flows of the game, underscored by a respect for the opponent without compromising their own ambitions."I love watching Barça, the way they play," Enrique said. "It's great to see the ambition and identity, which is similar to what we are looking for. But of course I would love to win tomorrow, as a Parisian, and we want to become the first team to beat Barça this season."
That balance of respecting the opponent while sticking true to each team's identity will be the theme of Tuesday's match, and is also the very reason why entertainment feels like a near guarantee. Enrique's task of neutralizing Yamal will be just as exciting for the tactics-obsessed observer as it will be for the more casual fan, in part because the only way Enrique's PSG know how to win is through an attack-minded approach. Similarly, Flick's attempts to overpower PSG's indomitable press will be entertaining regardless of what compelled you to turn the game on. The entertainment value is just as notable as each team's ambitions of winning the Champions League, a defining feature of an event that has the feeling of a big game even if the knockouts are months away.

Germie Bernard's breakout fuels Fantasy optimism, while Jameis Winston and Rhamondre Stevenson raise concerns entering Week 7

        We had some amazing performances in Week 6, but I wanted to highlight two players who stood out in Germie Bernard and Luther Burden III. And, unfortunately, let's discuss two players we were counting on who disappointed us in Rhamondre Stevenson and Jameis Winston.These are some of the biggest winners and losers from Week 6.Week 6 Fantasy WinnersSteelers WR Germie Bernard
Germie Bernard delivered an awesome performance at Tampa Bay after being a major waiver-wire target heading into the Week 6. Bernard had 11 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets, and he now has 17 catches for 167 yards and a touchdown on 21 targets in his past two outings. While Aaron Rodgers turned in a relatively moderate overall game that required overtime to build a solid final line (253 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception), the target distribution in this passing attack was exceptionally promising. Both Bernard and DK Metcalf (11 catches for 93 yards on 15 targets) saw excellent volume throughout the contest, creating strong optimism that Bernard's heavy role will persist for the remainder of the season, or at least until Roman Wilson (finger) and/or Michael Pittman (foot) return to action. Currently rostered in 76 percent of CBS Sports leagues and started in just 51 percent this past week, that start percentage should comfortably jump above 80 percent entering Week 7 against New Orleans.Bears WR Lurther Burden III
We wanted to see Caleb Williams (hamstring) come back after a three-game absence and feature his top receivers in Week 6 at Atlanta, and that's what happened for Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Burden had eight catches for 95 yards on eight targets, and Loveland had six catches for 65 yards and a touchdown in six targets. It was the best game for both with Williams, and hopefully that's a sign of things to come. We can't say the same about Rome Odunze, who only had three catches for 39 yards on four targets, but we're excited about Burden and Loveland heading into Week 7 against New England. Burden should be considered a No. 2 Fantasy receiver in the majority of leagues, and I'm ready to trust Loveland again as a starting Fantasy tight end.
Week 6 Fantasy LosersGiants QB Jameis Winston 
Jameis Winston's disastrous performance in Week 6 against the Saints might have cost him his job. He was 14-of-26 passing for 152 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, and he was benched in favor of JJ McCarthy, who almost led a comeback victory against New Orleans. McCarthy was 11-of-21 passing for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception, and he added two carries for 26 yards. We'll see who starts in Week 7 against Houston, but we can't trust Winston as a streaming option. Even if he starts against the Texans, he could get benched mid-game again if he struggles.Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson
Expectations were high for Rhamondre Stevenson early in Week 6 when it appeared like TreVeon Henderson would miss the game with a high ankle sprain. However, Henderson ultimately suited up against the Jets, and Cory Kiner ended up logging crucial high-value touches — including work on the final drive to milk the clock. The end result was a massive letdown for Stevenson, who managed just 36 yards on 14 carries (2.6 YPC) with zero involvement in the passing game. Henderson had seven carries for 31 yards and one catch for 9 yards on one target against the Jets, but he also lost a fumble. And Kiner finished with 11 carries for 57 yards and no targets. We'll see what happens in Week 7 against the Bears, but Stevenson should be considered a low-end No. 2 Fantasy running back in most leagues after what happened in Week 6.

        Week 6 wraps up in Santa Clara, where the Washington Commanders will visit the San Francisco 49ers for a "Monday Night Football" showdown. As Washington tries to inch closer to .500 on the season and rid itself of the sour taste of a tie with the Giants last week, it will have one of its key weapons on offense. The status of Stefon Diggs was up in the air for this primetime matchup as the wideout dealt with a hamstring injury, but he is active. Diggs did not practice at the start of the week on Thursday, but returned to practice in a limited capacity on Friday and Saturday. Officially, he was listed as questionable.Diggs, who signed a one-year deal with the franchise in early August, did not play in last week's tie with New York because of that hamstring.

When healthy, the 32-year-old has been a heavily involved figure within the Commanders offense, averaging just under eight targets per game so far this season. Because Terry McLaurin has also been in and out of the lineup due to injury, Diggs actually leads the team in targets (31), receptions (18), and receiving touchdowns (3). His 170 receiving yards are second to McLaurin (203). What's fascinating about Diggs' tenure so far in Washington is that he's seen minimal time playing with quarterback Jayden Daniels. Because of injuries, there's only been one full game played between the two. That came in the season-opening loss to Philadelphia, where Diggs caught four of nine targets for 55 yards and a touchdown. Before Daniels left Week 2's loss to the Cowboys with a left elbow injury, the two connected for another touchdown. If/when these two can stay healthy and be on the field at the same time, they've flashed some explosiveness. 
That'll be extremely important in this NFC matchup as the 49ers defense has been one of the stoutest in the league entering Week 6. San Francisco has the lowest explosive play rate allowed through five games by any team since 2000. Having a healthy Diggs would go a long way in putting a dent into that historic figure.

title: Colts' fire GM Chris Ballard: What fire sale could look like if Indy trades DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, others - CBS Sports
description: The Colts don't have a 2027 first-round pick. But what could they get for top veterans in preparation for a 2027
body:
The Colts don't have a 2027 first-round pick. But what could they get for top veterans in preparation for a 2027 rebuild?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chris Ballard era as the Indianapolis Colts general manager came to an end on Monday. A 26-20 home loss against the previously 0-5 Tennessee Titans in Week 6 was enough for Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon to pull the plug on Ballard six games into his 10th season on the job.Under Ballard, Indianapolis reached the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips. The Colts' 72-82-1 regular season record under his management ranked 17th in the league during Ballard's tenure. Indianapolis's five missed playoffs in a row (since 2021) is the Colts' longest such streak since 1988 to 1994, and the team never won an AFC South title under Ballard.Now, the franchise is left to pick up the pieces with a 2027 rebuild on the horizon. The good news is that the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most talented in years. The bad news is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, as well as wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, to the New York Jets in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner last season.However, there are multiple ways for Indianapolis to recoup draft capital through veterans on tradable deals. Let's take a look at what a potential fire sale of three of the Colts' top players could look like. 
DT DeForest Buckner
Three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner all but demanded a trade after the team's Week 6 loss against the Tennessee Titans. "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday.   At 32 years old, Buckner still has plenty of gas in the tank. His 4.0 sacks through six weeks are tied for the 10th most in the NFL, while his 19 quarterback pressures rank as the seventh most among defensive tackles in 2026. The Colts would be unwise not to make him available, as he is set to become a free agent in the 2027 offseason. What could his market look like?
For a player at his age and contract status, this could be one of his last prime seasons, but for legitimate contenders, that could be worth a third-or fourth-round pick. Teams who could be interested could include the Green Bay Packers (4-2), the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0). The Packers lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave for the season with a torn Achilles, so it would make sense for them to place a call for Buckner. The 49ers make too much sense. That's where Buckner played his first four seasons, culminating in the 49ers losing Super Bowl LIV to the Kansas City Chiefs to conclude the 2019 season. He was traded to the Colts for a first-round pick in the 2020 offseason. San Francisco is going through its regularly scheduled injury catastrophe, which has hit their defensive line hard. If the Vikings want a mentor for rookie first-round pick Caleb Banks and another high-level contributor for defensive coordinator Brian Flores to get creative with, they would make sense as a win-now team. LG Quenton Nelson
Colts left guard Quenton Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler and a three-time first-team All-Pro, is primed to be one of the NFL's most coveted free agents next offseason ahead of his 31st birthday on March 19. This season, Nelson is currently Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard in the entire NFL with an 89.2 offensive grade. 
He is a big fish who could net the Colts a second-round pick or perhaps a first-round choice if the bidding for his services gets frisky at the trade deadline. The complication is that he would be a rental or someone who would demand a top-of-the-market extension for whoever trades for his services. Who could line up for him? The Packers, a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued front, have stabilized their offensive line with the same starting five combination. But they could be in the mix, since they're currently rolling with aging veterans they signed off the street to start for them. If the Houston Texans (2-4), winners of two in a row, continue to climb, perhaps they would be interested. However, their asking price could be higher since they're a fellow AFC South team. The Vikings could be interested if they want to upgrade for undrafted free agent Joe Huber at left guard, with Donovan Jackson out with a torn meniscus. The 49ers, who are currently starting 2025 seventh-round pick Connor Colby at left guard, could make an all-in trade for Nelson. 
RB Jonathan Taylor 
The Colts don't need to trade three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor. He is still just 27 years old, and he re-signed with Indianapolis on a two-year extension worth $44 million with $39 million in total guarantees in August. However, if the Colts want to jumpstart their rebuild in earnest, parting with Taylor now could perhaps net them a first-round pick. They could point toward the impact top-end running backs Kenneth Walker III, Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs and others are having all around the league as reason to demand a 2027 or a 2028 first-round pick in return.Indianapolis could perhaps engage two AFC North teams, the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) and the Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2), in a bidding war. The Bengals are averaging the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (82.8) in the entire league this season, while Aaron Rodgers could use more support for the Steelers' 13th-worst running game (99.2 rushing yards per game) in what appears to be his NFL swan song. The Packers trading a 2028 first and another pick or two for Taylor could give them the runway to release Josh Jacobs after some legal trouble landed him on the commissioner's exempt list for the first six weeks of the 2026 season. They rank dead last in the league in rushing (59.8 rushing yards per game), and Taylor is a former Wisconsin Badger. Trading for him would earn them public relations bonus points by dumping Jacobs and bringing a local product home.

title: Dalton Knecht waived by Lakers: Why the 2024 draft class was doomed from the start (and the No. 1 pick) - CBS Sports
description: The 2023 NBA Draft featured Victor Wembanyama, who many already consider the best player in the world. The 2025 Draft had an epic tank b
body:
The 2023 NBA Draft featured Victor Wembanyama, who many already consider the best player in the world. The 2025 Draft had an epic tank battle to "Capture the Flagg" in order to secure Cooper Flagg. And of course, the 2026 Draft — despite none of the players playing a single regular-season minute yet — has the potential to go down as one of the greatest classes in NBA history.Between those draft classes, you have the 2024 Draft. In the months leading up to the event, it was, at least on paper, viewed as an underwhelming class compared with previous years and the drafts to follow. It lacked both consensus and blue-chip talent, unlike the top of the 2023, 2025, and 2026 classes.Through the first two seasons, the data doesn't lie. Four lottery picks from the class have already been traded, including No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher. Kel'el Ware and Jared McCain, the No. 15 and 16 picks in the draft, respectively, were also traded, albeit for different reasons. 
        
            
                Ranking the NBA's top 100 players: Victor Wembanyama enters 2026-27 season at No. 1
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
And Dalton Knecht, who showed promise during his lone season at Tennessee in 2023-24 as a potential draft riser, was waived by the Lakers on Monday, according to ESPN. Knecht had been in trade rumors since his rookie season, which included a botched trade at the 2024 trade deadline that would've seen him go to the Hornets in exchange for Mark Williams.
While yes, this class hasn't exactly been Hall of Fame-worthy, there have been some bright spots. Stephon Castle looks like a legitimate star. Donovan Clingan, Alex Sarr, and Zach Edey are all starting-level bigs in the NBA. Matas Buzelis would probably go top 5 in a re-draft. And you can't forget about the steal of the draft: Ajay Mitchell. The Thunder guard was one of the stars of the 2026 playoffs and checked in at No. 86 in our CBS Sports Top 100 NBA player list. Sarr (No. 94), Castle (No. 40), and Mitchell were the lone members of the 2024 draft class who cracked the list.With so much uncertainty surrounding the class, let's dive into what went wrong, what's next, and why this class can be a cautionary tale for next summer's draft.
Why the uncertainty of the class started at No. 1 with AtlantaOnly three No. 1 overall picks this century have been traded before the start of their third NBA season. Risacher is one of them, and he isn't in exactly prestigious company.Anthony Bennett (2013): To this day, Bennett going No. 1 is one of the most shocking moments in draft history. The UNLV big man appeared in just 52 games for the Cavaliers before being traded to the Timberwolves. The 2013 Draft remains the lowlight of this century. Then again, the Bucks selected a teenager from Greece named Giannis Antetokounmpo with the No. 15 pick. It's safe to say that pick worked out well.Markelle Fultz (2017): After playing just 33 total regular-season games with the 76ers, Fultz was traded to the Magic. He spent five seasons in Orlando, then moved on to the Kings (21 games) and Raptors (5) and is currently unsigned. Fultz was picked ahead of the likes of Jayson Tatum (No. 3), De'Aaron Fox (No. 5), Lauri Markkanen (No. 7), Donovan Mitchell (No. 13) and Bam Adebayo (No. 14).Zaccharie Risacher (2024): There was debate about what the Hawks would do in the weeks leading up to this draft. The three options were Risacher, Sarr and Reed Sheppard. Notably, Sarr did not work out with the Hawks, which cleared the way for Atlanta to make Risacher the pick. He was traded after just two seasons to the Mavericks, where he will team up with Flagg, the No. 1 overall pick selected the year after him.Risacher wasn't exactly a can't-miss prospect. The 6-foot-8 wing had the archetype and upside as a shooter that NBA decision-makers covet, but it just didn't work for him in Atlanta. After a promising rookie season during which he averaged 12.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and shot 35.5% from the 3-point line on 4.6 attempts per game, his overall volume decreased as a sophomore.During the first round of the playoffs against the Knicks, Risacher found himself out of the rotation after Game 1 and played just 22 total minutes across three games. The writing was on the wall, given Atlanta's plethora of players at the same position, and Risacher was be the odd man out.
Now, Risacher will try to revive his career in his second act with the Mavericks. If there is any consolation prize, new Mavericks coach Dusty May has experience working with jumbo lineups, which could bode well for Risacher. During his final season at Michigan, May started three frontcourt players: Aday Mara, Morez Johnson Jr., and Yaxel Lendeborg. The year before that, Michigan was the only team in college basketball that started two 7-footers: Danny Wolf and Vlad Goldin.
May unlocked the best in that trio and helped those players become lottery picks. With Wolf and Goldin, Michigan went from the bottom of the Big Ten to the Sweet 16 in May's first season at the high-major level. In Dallas' final preseason game, May rolled out an even larger starting lineup of Kyrie Irving, Risacher, Flagg, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford. While it's unclear if Risacher will be a long-term option at the 2 in that lineup, May's experience working with unorthodox lineups could bode well for the former No. 1 overall pick to establish a clear-cut role heading into his third NBA season.
A failed trade was the beginning of the end for Knecht in L.A.On Nov. 19, 2023, Knecht had a breakout performance against the Utah Jazz in the NBA Cup, knocking down nine 3-pointers and finishing with 37 points in 38 minutes during a dramatic 124-118 win. That moment should've been viewed as a coming-out party that established him as a key member of L.A.'s rotation for years to come.Instead, it was the beginning of the end. Less than three months later, Knecht was included in a trade package — alongside picks — to land Mark Williams from Charlotte. The trade came days after the Lakers stunned the NBA world by acquiring Luka Dončić in a deal that sent Anthony Davis back to Dallas. The trade for Williams — which cost the Lakers their promising rookie — was to give Dončić a long-term answer at the center position.But the trade was rescinded days later after Williams failed a physical exam with the Lakers. From that moment on, Knecht's career and outlook with the Lakers were murky at best. He has been a constant fixture in the trade rumor mill since almost being traded to Charlotte and has floated in and out of the Lakers' rotation.
On the days before the 2024 Draft, I thought Knecht being a top 10 pick was one of the lone guarantees from a class with plenty of unknowns. Knecht was the best transfer in college basketball during the 2023-24 season and established himself as one of the top shot creators and shooters in the class. On draft night, though, Knecht slid all the way to pick No. 17. At the time, he was considered one of the steals of the year. Knecht did struggle in summer league weeks later, but the signs from the start of his rookie year backed up the claim that he would outperform his draft slot.After appearing in just 54 games (and averaging just over 10 minutes per contest), that no longer appears to be the case. When asked about Knecht's future ahead of the Lakers' final preseason game, JJ Redick was blunt when asked what had changed since his rookie season."I think the biggest thing is the team changed," Redick said last week. "The team changed. Needs changed, the fit changed. I think he's gotten better as a player the last two years. I think, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the injuries we had. I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he's in a tough spot right now."
Why did teams move on from their rookies so quickly?From the first top 20 picks of the 2024 Draft, seven players have been traded or cut. However, there is no one-size-fits-all reason why a team decided to trade said player.Zaccharie Risacher (No. 1): He wasn't going to be part of the rotation going forward. The writing was on the wall after a shaky postseason.Rob Dillingham (No. 8): Dillingham has already been traded twice in 2026. The Timberwolves sent the one-time Kentucky star to the Bulls at the deadline. Then he was flipped again last month to the Hornets before being waived. It just hasn't worked out for Dillingham, an undersized guard who can't shoot. He remains a free agent heading into the season.Cody Williams (No. 10): Williams was a promising prospect coming out of Colorado. The younger brother of Thunder star Jalen Williams received some buzz as a potential No. 1 pick in a wide-open class due to his archetype. However, he was never able to find a consistent role with Utah and was traded to Minnesota earlier this offseason.Devin Carter (No. 13): Carter's rookie season got off to a rough start. After undergoing shoulder surgery right after the draft, Carter didn't play in the summer league or preseason and missed the start of the 2023-24 season. Carter was buried in Sacramento's guard rotation and never found consistent minutes. He was salary-dumped to the Hawks earlier this offseason before being waived. Carter is now on a two-way deal with the Celtics.Kel'el Ware (No. 15): Ware has shown flashes of being one of the best players from the class throughout his time with Miami. Now, he will look for a fresh start in Milwaukee after being part of the blockbuster trade that sent Antetokounmpo to the Heat.Jared McCain (No. 16): Former 76ers general manager Daryl Morey said they "sold high" on McCain when they traded him to Oklahoma City. McCain's rookie season with Philadelphia got off to a fantastic start before suffering a season-ending injury. McCain kept it up with the Thunder and is one of the best players from the class.Dalton Knecht (No. 17): Knecht was considered one of the most NBA-ready players in the class. He has lived up to that bill, at times, but inconsistent minutes with the Lakers — and the failed trade to Charlotte — were indicative of what was to come.One notable player who is set to be on his team's roster on Opening Night is former No. 6 pick Tidjane Salaün. The Hornets needed to cut one player to reach the 15-man roster limit and decided to waive veteran guard Pat Connaughton instead. Salaün was projected to go late-lottery on draft night. Instead, Charlotte selected him with the No. 6 pick. The phrase "two years away from being two years away" applies to Salaün, although he has shown signs of growth throughout his career. He is still just 21, but it's still a long shot that he plays meaningful minutes for the Hornets this season.Is there still hope for the 2024 class?Our CBS Sports Top 100 rankings tell the story about the stars of this class. Castle is part of a title contender with the Spurs and has the claim as the best — and most accomplished — player in the class so far. Mitchell, though, looks primed for a larger role with Oklahoma City this season and has legit breakout potential after a fantastic postseason.
Sarr looks like an ideal fit alongside Anthony Davis in Washington's frontcourt. His calling card in the pre-draft process was his defense, and he has certainly met expectations on that front: he averaged 2 blocks and 0.8 steals last season and could be in line to increase those numbers this season.Another player in this class who has flown under the radar is Jaylen Wells. The former second-round pick — who was selected right after Mitchell — started 69 games for Memphis last season and averaged 12.5 points, 3.2 assists, and 1.6 rebounds. Notably, Wells was the lone second-round pick to land on an All-Rookie team.The player to keep an eye on this season is Sheppard, who was thrown into a larger role last season after Fred VanVleet suffered a season-ending torn ACL weeks before the start of the 2025-26 campaign. Sheppard appeared in all 82 regular-season games and made 21 starts. He also started five of Houston's six playoff games, but averaged just under 30% from the 3-point line on 54 total attempts.
Sheppard's calling card coming out of Kentucky was his shooting. He was arguably the best 3-point shooter in college basketball during his lone college season. He did take strides from his rookie season (33.8%) to his sophomore year (39.4%) in the NBA from beyond the arc, but his first two seasons have been inconsistent for a former top-three pick.With Houston getting VanVleet back, it should take some of the pressure off Sheppard, but this will be an important year, as he is eligible for a rookie-scale extension next summer.Is the 2024 Draft a cautionary tale for next summer's draft?Major lottery reform is coming to the NBA this season. The new 3-2-1 format is designed to combat tanking and make the regular season more competitive after an epic tank race last season that saw the Wizards, Jazz, Grizzlies and Bulls jump into the top four.
There are plenty of unknowns about how the 2027 NBA Draft will ultimately stack up, but the early returns suggest NBA fans and teams should keep an eye on 2028 as the class that will be worth being "bad" for. Names to know for 2027 include Kansas' Tyran Stokes, Arkansas' Jordan Smith Jr. and Arizona's Caleb Holt. All great players, but it will be hard to rival what we witnessed last year —and even in 2025 — as far as draft classes go.Does that mean the 2027 Draft will have the same lack of consensus as 2024? Maybe. It's far too early to tell. Stokes is the consensus No. 1 prospect in the 2027 class heading into the season. However, if Duke big man Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje were eligible for the 2027 Draft — and he's not because he doesn't meet the draft's age requirement — the 7-foot-2 forward would be the consensus top-ranked prospect.
        
            
                2027 NBA Mock Draft: Tyran Stokes, Jordan Smith Jr., Stefan Joksimovic headline top picks before season starts
                
                    Adam Finkelstein                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
After back-to-back stacked draft classes, this upcoming draft could rival the 2024 class, but it's far too early to tell. The teams that got lottery luck in 2025 and 2026 should be thanking their lucky stars. The Hawks, unfortunately, won the lottery in a draft class that probably only stacks up to 2013.It's why Risacher is already on a new team and several others in the class have been traded. The 2024 class was set up to fail from the jump, and history suggests it might not get much better.

title: U.S. Open Cup final: Josef Martinez embraces chance at turning Crew's tide - CBS Sports

        With nine trophies in their history, the Columbus Crew are among the most successful teams in Major League Soccer, but it has been two years since their last trophy, as much of the team has shifted and wasn't involved in their last trophy, a Leagues Cup win in 2024. Now, as they gear up to host the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup final on Wednesday against St. Louis City SC (live on Paramount+ and CBS Sports Network, 8 p.m. ET), it's a chance to salvage the season, and there are still players there who have experience winning, even in this competition.During the summer, forward Josef Martinez joined the club after what he described as a tough time with Club Tijuana in Liga MX. While at the moment, it was a move that felt like it should be made leaving CF Montreal, sometimes those moves don't work out, but Martinez is also grateful to be with the Crew currently, where he has been able to get back to full fitness and have a chance to contribute now with the chance to win a trophy."We have to recognize that this is an opportunity to turn on the little bit of a struggle season; this is the opportunity to win something," Martinez said. "I have had the opportunity to win one time; I lost one in Miami, and this is my third one. So, it's special when you have a final. I don't remember how many players have the opportunity to play that."Martinez won the Open Cup with Atlanta United in 2018 while also capturing the Golden Boot, MLS Cup, and MVP awards all in that same season. Things haven't gone as expected recently with the Crew being his fifth team in the past three years but that doesn't mean that the 33-year-old Venezuelan doesn't have something to offer the squad both on and off the pitch as they look to secure their first trophy post-Wilfried Nancy. And no matter what, that's a moment worth looking forward to.
"A final is special, man. It's an opportunity to win something with the club. That is the most important right now," Martinez said, summing up the occasion.This isn't something that the Crew will need extra motivation for, as when you're playing a sport that you love, the goal is to get to a moment like this. Martinez may have already etched his name in MLS history, but for many on the team, they'll be looking to him and Mendez to set an example on Wednesday. It's something that Martinez is aware of, and it's a role that he relishes as a veteran of the league. He came to Atlanta to prove that he could make it and became "El Rey" (The king) for a reason, and even at his age, he's still a forward who strikes fear into the opposition, even if they're unbeaten in 22 straight games like St. Louis are."We're professional," Martinez said. "We know what the game is; we know what the situation is right now. And we know that is important. We have to go there and play soccer and fight. That's most important. We play soccer. We don't play any other sport. We have pressure; but they have pressure too. So, I think [who] makes fewer mistakes, they can have the opportunity to win."
Being able to deal with that pressure is something that Martinez brings to this squad, which has undergone plenty of change. The Crew may not make the playoffs as they're 11th in the Eastern Conference, so they'll need to look at this as a moment that will make or break their season. But when looking across the pitch, St. Louis City SC have never been in a final in their history so the pressure will be felt both ways but Martinez's goals can make the difference."Yeah, we're happy [to be in the final], man. When we score, we strikers want to score every game," Martinez said. "And we get frustrated when we can't do, we can't do not that. But it's a game. We have to be ready for all of this. And that will be a tough game because they are a really good team."Martinez will have the squad ready for the task at hand as it's a moment where both he and the Crew can get back to their best while being able to host a final in front of their home fans. You can't ask for a better chance than this in what will be an excellent final.

title: Rams special teams woes continue: Kicker Blake Grupe placed on injured reserve after knee injury - CBS Sports
description: Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
body:
Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Rams' kicking conundrum continued into Week 6, but not in the way you'd expect. After cutting former placekicker Harrison Mevis after Week 5, L.A. seemingly found its solution after signing Blake Grupe to assume the kicking duties. The former Notre Dame kicker made his Rams debut on Sunday and quickly endeared himself to his new squad by netting a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter. However, things went downhill after that. Grupe left the game early after suffering a knee injury on a kickoff. On Monday, the Rams placed him on injured reserve, leaving them once again looking for a kicker. Head coach Sean McVay said Grupe tore his ACL.Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on the kickoff following his made field goal. He was seen lowering his shoulder to hit returner Devin Duvernay and came down awkwardly. 
With Grupe sidelined, the entire kicking operation was reshuffled. Punter Ethan Evans served as the kicker. He only attempted one kicker, a successful extra point after the Rams' fourth-quarter touchdown. 
However, otherwise, Los Angeles was hesitant to use Evans. After Matthew Stafford connected with Blake Corum for a 15-yard touchdown in the second quarter, they kept the offense on the field for a two-point attempt, which failed. Then, when they were at the Arizona 27-yard line and faced with a fourth-and-1, Los Angeles went for it, but turned the ball over on downs. Grupe entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2023, initially signing with the Saints. He played for New Orleans until midway through the 2025 season, when he was released. After that, he made stops with the Colts and Jets before finding his way to the Rams. Coming into this game, Grupe had converted 81.9% of his career field goals (86-of-105) and 98% of his extra points (96-of-98). 
The kicking game has been an issue throughout the first half of the season for the Rams, and it came to a head during Monday's overtime loss to the Bills. Mevis failed to convert on either of his field goal attempts, including what would've been a game-winner, which was blocked. That forced Los Angeles' hand to make a change in favor of Grupe, but this latest injury keeps them in a kicking nightmare.

title: John Harbaugh provides update on Giants' QB situation between JJ McCarthy, Jameis Winston - CBS Sports

McCarthy made his Giants debut on Sunday after Jameis Winston was benched

        John Harbaugh's first season as the New York Giants coach is once again dominated by his quarterback situation. First, it was the season-ending injury to Jaxson Dart. Now, it's a position battle between JJ McCarthy and Jameis Winston. The Giants initially turned to Winston after Dart suffered his injury in Week 2. As he is known to do, Winston has had good and bad moments over the past five games. He has played well enough, though, to post a 2-1-1 record as the Giants' starting quarterback. Winston struggled on Sunday, however, and he was replaced in the second half by McCarthy, who engineered three fourth-quarter scoring drives. The comeback fell short, however, as the Saints left New Jersey with a 34-27 win. Harbaugh, as expected, was asked on Monday if Winston would be his starting quarterback for the Giants' upcoming road game against the Houston Texans. "We're working through that now, homing in on a decision," Harbaugh said. 
Harbaugh's decision will be crucial for the Giants, who are currently in first place in the NFC East. Should they give Winston another shot, or is it time to see what McCarthy can do?Harbaugh is likely considering the opponent. The Texans, after an 0-4 start, have won two straight games after they defeated the Jaguars on Sunday in London. While this season hasn't been their best, the Texans have talented players on defense, especially pass rusher Will Anderson, who leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. While McCarthy's mobility may be an asset, his lack of experience running the Giants' offense could also hold the Giants back. Expect Harbaugh to give both quarterbacks reps during practice until a decision is made.   
Quarterback isn't the only position Harbaugh needs to address. He also needs to figure out who the Giants' starting running back is after Cam Skattebo — the Giants' starter on paper — inexplicably received zero carries during Sunday's loss to the Saints. Harbaugh said afterward that he is waiting for one of his running backs to earn the job.

title: SEC midseason grades: Kentucky posts 'A+', while Texas and Texas A&M disappoint - CBS Sports
description: There are a ton of good teams in the SEC, but is there an elite team capable of winning multiple College Football Playoff games this sea
body:
There are a ton of good teams in the SEC, but is there an elite team capable of winning multiple College Football Playoff games this season and ending the league's national title drought in January?That remains to be seen.As expected, this conference is beating itself up a bit with the move to a nine-game league schedule through the first half of the regular season. The SEC is one of two conferences within the Power Four without an unbeaten team entering Week 8, a product of the league being closer to the NFL model than any other nationally.There are nine SEC teams in the latest AP poll, but only two are situated inside the top 10. Handing out midseason grades for every squad is a lesson in futility since any team in the league could take out any other the rest of the way -- well, maybe not Arkansas or Vanderbilt.We've included every school's preseason and current ranking to reflect expectations and actual results.

        
            
                CBS Sports 138: Miami tops Ohio State, BYU for No. 1 spot in college football rankings
                
                    Chip Patterson                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 AlabamaRecord: 5-2, 3-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 13The Crimson Tide's once handsome start is beginning to fizzle, much like Keelon Russell's significance in the Heisman race. Alabama's sophomore quarterback has been quiet over his last two outings since the multi-touchdown explosion at Mississippi State on Oct. 3 pushed his team toward the top 5. The running game has improved this season, one of the promises Kalen DeBoer made this offseason, but Alabama has underwhelmed up front with the second-most sacks, pressures and tackles for loss allowed in the SEC. The negative plays hinder an offense that gets by on explosive plays and Russell's ingenuity, and have too often put Alabama's average defense back on the field. Grade: B
                            
    
                                                
                    
    ArkansasRecord: 3-4, 1-3 | Preseason AP ranking: N/ASomething has finally clicked for the Razorbacks over their last two SEC games, easily the best they've looked this season following a one-possession loss to Tennessee and Saturday's win over Vanderbilt. Maybe small strides are being made in Ryan Silverfield's first season, but this remains nowhere near where Arkansas wants to be as a program. Near the bottom of the SEC in total offense and scoring offense, the Razorbacks must find a way over the second half of the campaign to generate a level up in momentum entering 2027. With only one win right now against Power Four competition and five games left as likely betting underdogs, it could get uglier from here. Grade: D
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Auburn Record: 4-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/ANo one's projecting this team to reach the CFP, but it's obvious the Tigers are ahead of schedule under Alex Golesh after Saturday's win at Georgia. Auburn watched a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter evaporate before forcing a crucial turnover and winning anyway, a high-end level of confidence and execution the last few coaching regimes never experienced against the Bulldogs. In fact, in previous matchups of that magnitude, Auburn would've likely folded. The biggest shock for this team is being in the league's bottom tier defensively despite DJ Durkin's return. A couple stops during the 44-39 home loss to Florida on Sept. 19, and the Tigers might be ranked inside the top 20. Grade: B+

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 20 FloridaRecord: 5-2, 3-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThis campaign could've deteriorated quickly for the Gators if Jon Sumrall didn't personally challenge his team to show more fight in high-pressure situations. Florida trailed 17-3 over the weekend at Texas before spot starter Tramell Jones, and that offense pulled itself off the turf with the season on the line. As Sumrall said at a program in transition, progress will not always be smooth. We may not be as starry-eyed over Florida as we were when this team was unbeaten and ranked No. 8 after beating Ole Miss, but they can still get to the CFP with a strong finish and better play in the secondary. The Gators certainly look like a more well-rounded football team from the top down under the new staff. Florida's one of three SEC teams entering Week 8 with two ranked victories. Grade: B
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Georgia Record: 6-1, 4-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 3There's no sense of defensive invincibility with this Georgia team as in years past, but the Bulldogs still look like the class of college football's most competitive league at midseason. Passing the test at Alabama in Week 6 was a major victory for Kirby Smart, but he had his reservations entering the rivalry bout with Auburn, and his fears came to fruition as Georgia was out-muscled at the line of scrimmage and failed to overcome self-inflicted mistakes. Gunner Stockton is a fine quarterback when he's not asked to do too much. Playing from behind with this passing game is not a winning recipe for the Bulldogs. Grade: B+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 KentuckyRecord: 6-1, 4-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe only team I'm comfortable giving a superior grade through Week 7 in the SEC, Will Stein gave off Curt Cignetti vibes with a hint of arrogance at SEC Media Days, and he has backed up that talk with superior execution. Not all mid-summer takes age well, but this Kentucky team -- on paper -- had the ingredients to put together a special season with a couple breaks, and the Wildcats have finished the drill with a top-15 ranking up to this point. Kentucky leads the SEC in turnover margin and is the least penalized team in the league, two signs of being well-coached. While Georgia's the only league lock right now for the playoff, Kentucky might be the second-best team in the conference, and that's no exaggeration. Grade: A+

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 18 LSURecord: 5-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 11The loss at Ole Miss was predictable, if not expected given the hoopla surrounding Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford, but failing to beat Kentucky in Lexington as a 10-point favorite with a superior roster was stunning for the Tigers. More inexcusable was Kiffin's decision to punt on fourth-and-1 near midfield with a chance to ice the game in the fourth quarter. A rookie head coach on the other sideline looked like the seasoned vet, comparatively. Defensively, LSU has looked terrific under Blake Baker's leadership. The Tigers are No. 1 in total defense and in run defense against conference foes, and should be favored in November to beat Alabama and Texas in Baton Rouge. Win those two games and others to reach the CFP, and this satisfactory showing goes to exemplary quick for Kiffin. Grade: C+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mississippi StateRecord: 4-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe Bulldogs had a cup of tea inside the top 25 following their 4-0 start, but then the Alabama debacle happened, during which quarterback Kamario Taylor and Fluff Bothwell got banged up and had to miss the showdown at LSU over the weekend. Consecutive humiliating losses in the conference have been humbling Jeff Lebby and his crew, who take on Oklahoma and Texas to finish out October. A promising start to the season now looks like Mississippi State will be scraping to hit seven wins. Considering preseason win total projections, however, it's a move in the right direction for a program that's already recorded more conference victories (2) this season than it had in the previous two years combined. Grade: B-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 22 MissouriRecord: 5-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 25It's critical that the Tigers are able to flush Saturday's 28-point loss at Ole Miss and simply move on. The open date comes at a great time for Missouri, ahead of a stretch run featuring Texas, Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma over the final month. Most physicality-geared teams like the Tigers would struggle with their Doak Walker candidate unavailable throughout the first seven games, but Jamal Roberts has 867 yards and eight touchdowns in relief of Ahmad Hardy and Missouri hasn't missed its top offensive weapon. If Missouri can get to nine wins, that might be enough to reach the CFP and torch preseason expectations from outside the program. Grade: B

                            
    
                                                
                    
    OklahomaRecord: 3-3, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 10A win over previously top-ranked Texas was supposed to put the Sooners back in business with Kentucky coming to Norman in Week 7. Didn't happen. Oklahoma's offense just can't get out of its own way with John Mateer at quarterback. The Sooners lead the SEC in turnovers (14) and rank last in total offense. This was an issue last season too, though not as critical. The Week 2 road loss at Michigan hasn't aged as well as most of us thought it would, either. The Wolverines only have one Big Ten win this fall. One guarantee with a Brent Venables-coached team continuing to hold true? This defensive group makes you earn everything. Grade: C-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 Ole MissRecord: 5-1, 3-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 9No grading on a curve here, folks. I can't overlook the 50-burger Florida hung on the Rebels a few weeks ago, but credit to Pete Golding and his staff for fixing defensive-wide issues during the open date that came thereafter. Ole Miss has blown out its consecutive league opponents (Vanderbilt and Missouri) but, surprisingly, is not favored to beat Texas on the road in Week 8. This looks like another double-digit-win season for a program that is proving Lane Kiffin was not the primary reason for its success. It's still about the players and leaders like Trinidad Chambliss. Grade: B+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    South CarolinaRecord: 3-3, 1-3 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe toughest team to evaluate at this point, the Gamecocks flunked their first three SEC exams this season under Shane Beamer before acing their trip to Florida last time out. Nothing about that performance made sense, except that South Carolina's execution finally lived up to its talent. The Gamecocks lead the SEC in rushing under new OC Kendal Briles, and LaNorris Sellers is coming off a five-touchdown outing. Problems have been blown leads, lack of consistency in the passing game, and occasional breakdowns in the secondary that lead to points. South Carolina's one of the brightest students in the class, but doesn't have the work ethic to match its potential. Grade: D+

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 TennesseeRecord: 6-1, 3-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 20The best defensive staff hiring of the SEC this season, Josh Heupel's courting of Jim Knowles has paid off big for the Vols. While the passing game works out the kinks with two different quarterbacks, Tennessee's defense has been its calling card in SEC play. The league's top-ranked scoring defense, the Vols also lead the conference in sacks and tackles for loss and have allowed the fewest touchdown passes (3). Tennessee has taken full advantage of its home schedule with wins over Auburn and Alabama and still has dates with Kentucky and LSU. The Vols' only loss was a three-point setback at Neyland Stadium to Texas, after the Longhorns tallied 10 sacks against Faizon Brandon. Grade: A
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 19 TexasRecord: 5-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 5A satisfactory score on midterms is not what anyone associated with Texas football expected this fall, not after the Longhorns spent more than $40 million assembling a roster headlined by Arch Manning, Colin Simmons and a wealth of talented transfers. There's no easy fix for an offense that ranks 15th in the SEC in explosive plays, 13th in rushing and 11th in passing and struggles to sustain drives. It's not like consecutive losses to Oklahoma and Florida exposed hairline cracks, either. Texas was outplayed by Ohio State for three quarters in the Longhorns' Week 2 win over the Buckeyes and needed to ask its dominant defense to yield one more stop in a 20-17 win at Tennessee. Few teams nationally have multiple wins over nationally ranked opponents like Texas, but the Longhorns would be unbeaten right now and not fighting for their playoff lives with five games left if Steve Sarkisian had things figured out offensively when the signs were there early. Grade: C

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas A&MRecord: 4-3, 1-3 | Preseason AP ranking: 8From preseason top 10 to unranked at midseason, the Aggies have been a disaster in SEC play outside of a win over Arkansas. Texas A&M was exposed at Kyle Field by Kentucky after an inflated 2-0 start, then got outscored by LSU and Missouri on the road, 62-12. Texas A&M was the overwhelming pick here at CBS Sports in August to be the SEC's most underwhelming team, so we nailed that one. Marcel Reed's regression at quarterback was obvious late last season despite the team's trip to the CFP, and replacing multiple offensive line starters in 2026 wasn't going to help. In four SEC starts as a junior, Reed has one touchdown pass and five interceptions. Grade: F
                            
    
                                                
                    
    VanderbiltRecord: 3-4, 0-4 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AThe Commodores were gifted a win against NC State, keeping them from being halfway to 10 losses after posting 10 wins last fall. Mind you, this was a confident group internally heading into the season, despite personnel losses and the plan to bring in five-star freshman quarterback Jared Curtis without restrictions. He's battling through growing pains during the team's current four-game skid, and it's not getting easier with a trip to Kentucky coming this weekend. If Vanderbilt doesn't find a way to upend Mississippi State in Starkville on Nov. 7, this is likely a winless campaign in SEC play for Clark Lea. Ouch. Grade: D

title: How Bronny James became the last survivor of Lakers' 2024 draft class -- and why that's not a good thing - CBS Sports
description: With his father on the 76ers, James still kept his Lakers roster spot over first-round pick Dalton Knecht
body:
With his father on the 76ers, James still kept his Lakers roster spot over first-round pick Dalton Knecht
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        On Monday, JJ Redick revealed that Bronny James and Dalton Knecht were both excused absences from practice on Monday. Both were ill, a statement The Athletic felt compelled to confirm in a follow-up report because, well, it seemed more like they both had a concerning case of Roster Bubble-itis. The Los Angeles Lakers spent most of the offseason with 16 players under standard contracts. Monday was the deadline to trim the roster down to 15, and the two likeliest candidates to get moved were their two 2024 draft picks.Redick himself said that he didn't think James played well in the preseason. He shot just 4-of-16 from the floor, and the Lakers lost his 82 minutes by 31 points. Yet the bar, apparently, was even lower, as it was ultimately Knecht, the No. 17 pick in that 2024 class, who was waived. All told, the pair of them and everything that has followed amounts to an abject disaster of a draft class for Rob Pelinka. Consider the following:Through two years, neither James nor Knecht have grown into NBA-caliber players. James, as a late-second round pick, was always fighting long odds. Knecht, frequently cited as the steal of that draft, was supposed to be a difference-maker early on. He entered the NBA as a 23-year-old coming off of an SEC Player of the Year season with a skill set that seemingly fit the existing roster to a tee. Aside from a few flashes early in his rookie year, he showed virtually nothing as a Laker.The Lakers tried to trade Knecht to the Charlotte Hornets. They called off the deal after failing Mark Williams' physical and could never move Knecht, or rebuild his confidence, afterward.Though they'd deny it, the Lakers surely drafted James, on some level, for the sake of preserving their relationship with his far more valuable father. Well, if Bronny was supposed to be a bridge between player and team, he failed on that front. LeBron James literally took a minimum-salary contract to play for somebody else.The Lakers didn't realize neither had a future with them quickly enough to move on last offseason when doing so would have allowed the flexibility to retain key defender Jordan Goodwin, who actually was an important part of the 2024-25 rotation and wound up breaking out for the Phoenix Suns after the Lakers let him go.The Lakers had a whole offseason to move either Knecht, James or someone else. They could have demanded it as a condition of trading nearly their entire cache of draft picks to the Utah Jazz for Walker Kessler. They could have signed one fewer free agent or made an aggregation trade. Instead, these picks went so badly that the Lakers were forced to take on the dead money that would come from waiving one of them. They couldn't even close the book on this miserable draft prooperly.At least to this point, the 2024 draft class has been a failure at every level. The Lakers picked the wrong players, developed them poorly and mismanaged the process of moving on from them. It's emblematic of many of the failures that have come under Pelinka. The Lakers land big-name players because they're the Lakers, and then they botch the margins around them.Why did the Lakers keep Bronny over Knecht?Why exactly James outlasted Knecht could come down to a number of factors. The more defensively oriented James is arguably the better fit on this offense-centric roster than Knecht, whose best trait is theoretically his shooting. James is undeniably the bigger name of the two just because of, well, his actual name. Technically speaking, the Lakers still have a LeBron James on their team. Neither played well in the preseason. We don't know what happened behind closed doors at training camp practices. James presumably outplayed Knecht there.
That doesn't mean he's proven he has an NBA future. At this point, it's getting harder and harder to believe that's the case. James simply is not an NBA-viable offensive player. Through two years, he has not proven capable of putting the ball through the hoop from anywhere on the court at the rate that a 6-foot-2 guard needs to in order to be playable. Even if he could hit the bare minimum number of shots to survive as a small, defense-first guard, it's not as though he's cleared the incredibly high bar a defender needs to in order to provide genuine value at that size. He is not a Jamal Shead-level pest. That's the standard at that size. James has never reached it.
Maybe that changes. Again, the Lakers have seen more of James, and Knecht for that matter, than we have, and it should be noted that James at least provided a handful of not-terrible minutes against the Houston Rockets in the playoffs a year ago. Development isn't linear. Maybe there's more to Bronny than we've thus far seen.
But when teams are forced to decide between two young and underwhelming players, the first-round pedigree, along with the greater cap number for the sake of trade flexibility, usually wins out. Even if there was more to the decision to keep James, it was fundamentally driven by how badly the Lakers mismanaged the Knecht situation. The Lakers bungled the 2024 draft so badly that a player who's done little to prove future NBA viability through two years had to make the team just because their other selection in that same class was worse. His continued presence on this roster, therefore, says far more about the team that drafted him than the player he's thus far become.

If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. Josef Newgarden won the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024 but Alex Palou won in 2025 and is the reigning champion.Can you bet on SuperCross?SuperCross is a type of motorcycle racing. Some sportsbooks do offer SuperCross odds in certain states.Can you bet on motocross at DraftKings?DraftKings does provide SuperCross odds, which is a motocross competition, in select states. You must be of legal age and residing in those states to bet on motocross at DraftKings.How to bet on F1?All major sportsbooks have lines available for F1 races. Many of the same types of bets available for NASCAR races are available for F1 events.

body:
C.J. Stroud and Woody Marks climb the Week 7 Fantasy projections, while Patrick Mahomes faces a tough matchup against Seattle
